content:
Apple announced updates to its Mac mini and Mac Studio models on the eve of its September event, catching many off guard. We had generally expected these announcements to be part of the event itself.

One plausible explanation is that the company wanted to clear these updates out of the way ahead of what promises to be a major 'Awe Dropping' keynote. But another new report offers a different theory…

Announcing new Mac mini and Mac Studio models two weeks before the September 9 event does seem surprising. Why not wait a fortnight and unveil them at the keynote rather than via a press release?

The Information reports that Apple made this decision because the company was caught off guard by the massive demand from AI applications, combined with some configurations being out of stock for months.

9to5Mac Opinion

There's no doubt that the power of Apple Silicon has made the Mac mini and Mac Studio popular choices for those wanting to run AI models locally. We've seen, for example, researchers using Thunderbolt 5 to combine four Mac Studios into a formidable AI cluster.

I also believe Apple didn't originally anticipate demand on this scale.

However, whether a two-week window would really make much difference seems unlikely. To me, the time gap is too small to be convincing. I personally find our earlier explanation more plausible.

Apple will be making a big deal of the launch of its first foldable iPhone, and it also needs to ensure the iPhone 18 Pro doesn't get overshadowed. If Apple launches the HomePad smart home hub as we expect, that would be another major announcement.

On top of that, there's a new Apple TV and HomePod mini 2 with Siri AI capabilities, two new Apple Watch models, and possibly new AirPods. With so much to announce in a single keynote, it's entirely understandable why Apple would want to get new Mac desktops out of the way first.

What do you think? Share your views in the comments.
